- Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) are privately pooled investment vehicles that collect funds 
from investors to invest in a variety of alternative asset classes. 
- AIFs cater to investors seeking exposure to non-traditional markets and higher-risk investments. AIFs in 
India are regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) under the SEBI (Alternative 
Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012. 
- These funds offer an alternative to traditional investment options like mutual funds, bonds 
and stocks, providing opportunities for higher returns and greater diversification. So, points I and III 
are not correct. 
- Types of AIFs are: 
o Private Equity funds 
o Hedge Funds. So, point II is correct. 
o Real Estate funds 
o Venture Capital funds. So, point IV is correct. 
o Infrastructure funds 
So, only two of the above are treated as Alternative Investment Funds. 
Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

- Article 366(1) of the Constitution of India provides that the expression ‘agricultural income’ in the 
Constitution means agricultural income as defined for the purpose of enactments relating to 
Indian Income Tax. 
- Taxes on agricultural income falls under Entry 46 in “State List” under the Constitution of 
India. Thus, only the State Governments are competent to enact legislations for taxation of agricultural 
income. The Central Government cannot levy income tax on agricultural income. However, agricultural 
income is considered for rate purposes while determining the income tax liability. 
- As per section 2(1A) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 ‘agricultural income’ means 
o Any rent or revenue derived from land which is situated in India and is used for agricultural 
purposes 
o Any income derived from such land by agricultural operations including processing of agricultural 
produce so as to render it fit for market or sale of such produce; 
o Any income attributable to a farm house subject to fulfilment of conditions specified in the Act; 
and 
o Any income derived from saplings or seedlings grown in a nursery 
- To sum up, for the purpose of Income Tax act, 1961 agricultural income is any rent or revenue 
by means of cash or in kind, derived from a land, which is used for an agricultural purpose 
and land should be situated in India. 
- The Supreme Court in the Commissioner of Income Tax vs. Raja Benoy Kumar Suhas Roy , 1957 
provided a definition for ‘agricultural processes’. In this judgement the court said that the mere fact that 
an activity has some connection with or is in some way dependent on land is not sufficient to bring it 
within the scope of the term and such extension of the term "agricult ure" is unwarranted. Therefore, 
activities like dairy farming, poultry farming, cheese & butter making or wool rearing

- Critical minerals are defined as a set of naturally occurring elements and compounds that have diverse 
irreplaceable industrial applications but confront supply-related vulnerabilities either in the form of their 
limited geographic occurrences or sourcing challenges. 
- The Mineral Security Partnership (MSP) is a US-led plurilateral partnership, which, according to its 
guiding principles, "strives to promote responsible growth across the critical minerals sector via a shared 
commitment to high Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) standards; sustainability; and shared 
prosperity." 
- The MSP currently consists of 23 partners, including Argentina, Australia, Canada, Estonia, Finland, 
France, Germany, Greenland, India, Italy, Japan, Kazakhstan, Mexico, Namibia, Norway, Peru, the 
Republic of Korea, Sweden, Ukraine, the UK, the US, Uzbekistan, and the EU (represented by the 
European Commission). So, statement I is correct. 
- Based on inter-ministerial consultations and adopted criteria which included the economic importance 
and supply chain risks associated with minerals, the Ministry of Mines identified and released a list 
30 critical minerals in June 2023. Out of these thirty elements, fourtee n have been highlighted for 
having both high economic importance as well as high supply risks. Seven have been categorized as 
elements of high supply risks and nine as elements with high economic importance. 
- As stated, supply chain vulnerabilities, formed one of the criteria for the listing of minerals. India did 
have significant reserves for some of the listed critical minerals like Copper, Graphite etc. 
but is largely import dependent for others like Antimony, Germanium etc . So, statement 
II is not correct.

- Circular economy refers to a system that aims 
to minimize the use of energy, natural resources 
and waste generation by closing loops of utilities 
and materials flows. It involves minimizing 
inputs of raw materials, reducing waste 
outputs and reintegrating products into the 
system when they reach the end of their 
life. 
- It works by extending product lifespan through 
improved design and servicing and relocating 
waste from the end of the supply chain to the 
beginning—in effect, using resources more 
efficiently by using them over and over, not 
only once. 
- In practice, it implies reducing waste to a minimum. When a product reaches the end of its life, its 
materials are kept within the economy wherever possible thanks to recycling. These can be productively 
used again and again, thereby creating further value.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements: Which of the statements given above are correct?

statements.label: I
statements.text: Capital receipts create a liability or cause a reduction in the assets of the Government

statements.label: II
statements.text: Borrowings and disinvestment are capital receipts

statements.label: III
statements.text: Interest received on loans creates a liability of the Government

explanations.explanation:
Statement I is correct: Capital receipts are those receipts of the government which create 
liability
 
or
 
reduce
 
ﬁnancial
 
assets.
 
 Statement II is correct: Borrowings—such as loans from the RBI, foreign governments, or 
through
 
the
 
issuance
 
of
 
government
 
securities—and
 
disinvestment,
 
which
 
entails
 
selling
 
the
 
government's
 
stake
 
in
 
public
 
sector
 
enterprises,
 
are
 
categorized
 
as
 
capital
 
receipts.
 
 Statement III is incorrect: Interest received on loans given by the Central government to the 
states
 
or
 
other
 
countries
 
is
 
classiﬁed
 
as
 
a
 
revenue
 
receipt
 
since
 
it
 
represents
 
income
 
for
 
the
 
government
 
and
 
d
oes
 
not
 
result
 
in
 
any
 
liability.

- In the balance of payment accounts, receipts are classified as capital or revenue. Capital receipts 
refer to incoming cash flows (receipts) originating from the sale of fixed assets, shares, or debt and are 
generally non-recurring. 
- Capital receipts leads to alteration in assets or liabilities of the receiver , on the other hand 
revenue receipts being day to day in nature are not asset or liability creating. So, statement I is 
correct. 
- Borrowings and disinvestment are classic examples of capital receipts. Borrowings lead to 
future repayment obligations, while disinvestment involves selling public assets, thus reducing 
government holdings. So, statement II is correct. 
- Interest received on loans is revenue income for the government and does not result in any 
liability. It is a return on the capital lent by the government and is thus a revenue receipt, not a capital 
one. So, Statement III is not correct. 
Therefore, option (a) is the correct answer.

- Raja Ram Mohan Roy was a central figure in the Indian Socio-Religious Reform Movement of the early 
19th century and is regarded as the first great leader of Modern India. 
- He studied Persian-Arabic literature, and later came under the influence of Vedic monism. He tried to 
improve Hinduism in the light of modern scient ific temper and logical thinking and issued 
a stinging criticism of idolatry, polytheism and clericalism. 
- Despite being critical of certain aspects of Hinduism Raja Ram Mohun Roy had great respects for 
traditional philosophical systems, to the extent that he advocated for reforms in Hinduism by going 
back to its purist form as enshrined in Vedanta text. So, statement I is correct. 
- Despite being an admirer of Western rationalism, scientific temper and enlightenment, he was equally 
critical of Western religio n as well. He only aspired for inculcating the rationalist, scientific 
approach of the west to bring the Indian society out of stagnation , so that human and dignity 
and social equality can be ensured for all men and women. So, statement II is correct. 
Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer.

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.label: D

explanations.explanation:
Option b is correct: In India, the irrigation device called araghatta or arahatta was one wheel 
with
 
pitchers
 
or
 
pots
 
of
 
clay
 
attached
 
around
 
the
 
rim
 
of
 
the
 
wheel.
 
It
 
was
 
also
 
called
 
‘Ghanti-Yantra’.
 
Araghatta
 
is
 
a
 
Persian
 
wheel,
 
a
 
mechanical
 
water-lifting
 
device,
 
used
 
in
 
medieval
 
India
 
to
 
lift
 
water
 
from
 
wells
 
for
 
irrigation.
 
 - The essential part of the araghatta was the ghati-yantra or the device with pitchers, 
usually
 
mounted
 
on
 
the
 
wheel,
 
but
 
not
 
attached
 
to
 
its
 
rim.
 
The
 
ghati-yantra
 
as
 
an
 
irrigation
 
device
 
is
 
therefore
 
often
 
held
 
as
 
a
 
pot
 
garland.
 
 - The araghatta seems to have drawn water from a reservoir which in turn received its 
water
 
from
 
an
 
irrigation
 
well.
 
The
 
spokes
 
(arakas)
 
of
 
a
 
wheel
 
was
 
a
 
revolving
 
apparatus
 
though
 
it
 
does
 
not
 
refer
 
to
 
any
 
gearing
 
mechanism
 
enabling
 
the
 
conversion
 
of
 
the
 
horizontal
 
rotary
 
motion
 
into
 
a
 
vertical
 
rotary
 
motion.
 
The
 
latter

which
 
became
 
visible
 
from
 
the
 
fourteenth
 
century
 
onwards,
 
represented
 
the
 
typical
 
Persian
 
wheel
 
or
 
the
 
saqia.

- The word ‘araghatta’ comes from the combination of two words ‘ ara;’ meaning spokes, and ‘ghatta’ 
meaning pot. Therefore, araghatta becomes a system of spokes with a pot at the end. 
- Araghatta was an irrigation device, with a rope-pot system of lifting water from open wells. In the 
modern English literature, it is referred to as Persian wheel, probably because of its first discovery by 
European historians in Persia, but the use of araghatta in India dates past the use in Persia. 
Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

- The Mauryans maintained an illustrio us and elephantine bureaucracy, right from the central to district 
level. This bureaucracy was further illustrated during the Ashokan times, when the empire reached its 
territorial zenith . 
- Ashokan inscriptions suggest that the pradeshika, rajuka, and yukta were important officers 
at the district level. 
- Rock edict 3 refers to these officers going on tours every five years in order to instruct 
people in dhamma and for other purposes. 
- The term rajuka may come from rajju, meaning rope, and the reference may be to the measurement of 
land using ropes. Though land measurement may have been their main or original duty, in 
Ashoka's time, the rajukas seem to have been high -ranking officers who were also 
associated with public welfare measures. Ashoka added judicial functions and dhamma propagation 
to their duties. 
- The term yukta occurs in the Arthashastra as a general term for officers, during the Ashokan times 
yuktas assisted the sthanikas and gopas in revenue collection. 
Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

- North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) , is a cold war era military alliance established in 
1949 between the Western European and North American countries (USA and Canada) that sought to 
create a counterweight to Soviet armies stationed in central and eastern Europe after World War II. 
- It is a collective security agreement, wherein any armed attack o n any of the participating country is 
taken as attack on all of the NATO members. 
- Article 10 of the North Atlantic Treaty sets out how countries can join the Alliance. It states 
that membership is open to any "European State in a position to further the principles of this Treaty and 
to contribute to the security of the North Atlantic area". 
- Any decision to invite a country to join the Alliance is taken by the North Atlantic Council, 
NATO's principal political decision-making body, on the basis of consensus among all Allies. 
- NATO currently has 32 members across Europe and North America - the original 12 founders 
plus 20 countries which have joined since 1949. After the Soviet Union's collapse in 1991, many Eastern

questions.stem: Which of the following are the evidences of the phenomenon of continental drift? Which of the following are the evidences of the phenomenon of continental drift? I. The belt of ancient rocks from Brazil coast matches with those from Western Africa. II. The gold deposits of Ghana are derived from the Brazil plateau when the two continents lay side by side. III. The Gondwana system of sediments from India is known to have its counterparts in six different landmasses of the Southern Hemisphere. Select the correct answer using the code given below:

statements.label: I
statements.text: The belt of ancient rocks from Brazil coast matches with those from Western Africa

statements.label: II
statements.text: The gold deposits of Ghana are derived from the Brazil plateau when the two continents lay side by side

statements.label: III
statements.text: The Gondwana system of sediments from India is known to have its counterparts in six different landmasses of the Southern Hemisphere

explanations.explanation:
Statement 1 is correct. Radiometric dating techniques have conﬁrmed that the rock formations 
along
 
the
 
eastern
 
coast
 
of
 
South
 
America
 
(Brazil)
 
and
 
the
 
western
 
coast
 
of
 
Africa
 
are
 
similar
 
in
 
age,
 
type,
 
and
 
structure.
 
This
 
is
 
one
 
of
 
the
 
most
 
compelling
 
geological
 
evidences
 
supporting
 
the
 
theory
 
of
 
continental
 
drift.
 Statement 2 is correct. Ghana, located on the west coast of Africa, has rich gold deposits along 
its
 
coast,
 
yet
 
there
 
is
 
no
 
local
 
source
 
rock
 
to
 
account
 
for
 
this
 
mineral
 
wealth.
 
The
 
likely
 
explanation
 
is
 
that
 
these
 
gold
 
deposits
 
originated
 
from
 
the
 
Brazil
 
Plateau
 
which,
 
before
 
the
 
continents
 
drifted
 
apart,
 
lay
 
adjacent
 
to
 
what
 
is
 
now
 
Ghana
.
 
This
 
is
 
one
 
of
 
the
 
pieces
 
of
 
evidence
 
supporting
 
the
 
theory
 
of
 
continental
 
drift.
 Statement 3 is correct. The Gondwana system of sedimentary rocks, particularly tillite deposits 
(sediments
 
formed
 
from
 
glacial
 
activity),
 
found
 
in
 
India,
 
have
 
strikingly
 
similar
 
counterparts
 
in
 
Africa,
 
Antarctica,
 
Australia,
 
Madagascar,
 
Falkland
 
Islands,
 
and
 
South
 
America.
 
These
 
similarities
 
provide
 
evidence
 
that
 
these
 
landmasses

part

supercontinent

- The Continental Drift Theory , proposed by Alfred Wegener in 1912, revolutionized our 
understanding of Earth’s geological history. It posits that continents were once united in a supercontinent 
called Pangaea and have since drifted apart over geological time. 
- He gave evidences in support of his theory as: 
o Similar rock types and structures are found on continents now separated by vast oceans. For 
instance, the Appalachian Mountains in North America align geologically with the Caledonian 
Mountains in Scotland and Scandinavia. 
o The matching ancient rock belts between Brazil and Western Africa are a well -
documented geological evidence of continental drift. These rocks share identical age, 
composition and structure, supporting the idea that South America and Africa were once joined. 
So, statement I is correct. 
o Geological studies suggest that the gold deposits in Ghana might have originated from 
the Brazilian Plateau, which aligns with the theory that the continents were once connected. 
So, statement II is correct. 
o The Gondwana sedimentary system found in India is also found in other southern 
landmasses like Africa, South America, Antarctica and Australia, providing strong 
evidence of past continental connection. So, statement III is correct. 
Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer.

(calcium carbonate). It is often associated with marine environments and is characterized by its 
distinctive white color and powdery texture. 
- It is primarily composed of the r emains of microscopic marine organisms known as coccolithophores. 
These organisms secrete calcium carbonate shells or plates, and when they die, their remains accumulate 
on the ocean floor. Over time, these accumulated remains can form thick layers of chalk rock. 
- Porosity and permeability of the soil depend on the particle size of the soil – if the sediments 
or rock particles are composed of very small grains, such as in clays and silts, the space through which 
water can flow is limited. In addition, clay particles have a lot of surface area to which hygroscopic water 
attaches, creating a further resistance to fluid movement.

coarser grains also have less surface area, so less water can attach to them, allowing better 
fluid movement. So, statement I is correct.

statement II is correct.

pore density, which varies with the moisture content of the soil. So, statement III is not 
correct.

- The atmosphere acts like a blanket of air around the earth. This implies that the atmosphere 
holds in the amount of heat needed to keep the earth liveable (Goldilocks’ planet). 
- In the atmosphere certain gasses like carbon dioxide, water vapour etc. are known to absorb the infrared 
radiation of the sun, thus preventing the temperature on the surface of earth to plummet in the absence 
of sun, that is during the night time. 
- Another way atmosphere maintains the temperature is by regulating the amounts of solar energy 
reaching the Earth, that is why the areas which has thicker layers of atmosphere (poles) receive lower 
solar energy, despite receiving equivalent radiation as the equatorial regions. 
- In the absence of atmosphere, the temperatures of the Earth’s surface will exhibit marked 
variations, reaching up to 100 degrees Celsius during the day, while plummeting to near freezing in the 
night, as is seen on the surface of the moon. This freezing effect would be more pronounced on 
the regions where the sun rays are incident at an angle (that is on poles and temperate regions) 
while the equatorial regions may have temperatures above the freezing point, as seen for the north pole 
and the south pole of the moon. So, statement I is not correct. 
- The greenhouse effect is the process through which heat is trapped near Earth's surface by 
certain gases, helping to maintain a warmer temperature than it would have otherwise. So, statement 
II is correct. 
- Greenhouse gases consist of carbon dioxide, methane, ozone, nitrous oxide, 
chlorofluorocarbons and water vapour. So, statement III is correct. 
Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

- Direct air capture (DAC) technologies extract carbon dioxide directly from the atmosphere at any 
location, unlike carbon capture which is generally carried out at the p oint of emissions, such as a steel 
plant. 
- This carbon dioxide can then be permanently stored in deep geological formations or used 
for a variety of applications, hence contributing to carbon sequestration . So, statement 1 is 
correct. 
- The captured carbon can then be used as a feedstock for various carbon-based materials. It 
can be used in the production of cement, plastics, food processing, carbon fibers, and other industrial 
applications. This helps keep carbon stored in the infrastructure, preventing its release into the

- Aviation is the most energy and carbon intensive mode of transport and the most difficult to decarbonise.

can help reduce carbon intensity of the sector in two ways, first is where continued use of fossil 
jet fuel is offset by capturing and sequestering CO2 from the atmosphere. The second is where carbon 
dioxide captured from the atmosphere is used as a feedstock, in conjunction with hydrogen 
from electrolysis, to produce a synthetic jet fuel. So, statement 3 is correct.

questions.stem: With reference to the Indian polity, consider the following statements: Which of the statements given above a are correct?

statements.label: I
statements.text: An Ordinance can amend any Central Act

statements.label: II
statements.text: An Ordinance can abridge a Fundamental Right

statements.label: III
statements.text: An Ordinance can come into effect from a back date

explanations.explanation:
Statement I is correct: As per Article 123 of the Constitution, the President can promulgate an 
ordinance
 
when
 
Parliament
 
is
 
not
 
in
 
session.
 
An
 
ordinance
 
has
 
the
 
same
 
force
 
and
 
effect
 
as
 
an
 
Act
 
of
 
Parliament,
 
and
 
thus,
 
it
 
can
 
amend
 
or
 
repeal
 
any
 
existing
 
Central
 
Act.
 Statement II is incorrect: An ordinance is subject to the same constitutional limitation as an act 
of
 
Parliament.
 
Hence,
 
an
 
ordinance
 
cannot
 
abridge
 
or
 
take
 
away
 
any
 
of
 
the
 
fundamental
 
rights
 Statement III is correct: As an ordinance has the same force and effect as an Act of 
Parliament,
 
ordinance
 
can
 
come
 
into
 
effect
 
from
 
a
 
back
 
date
 
as
 
the
 
retrospective
 
law.

- Article 123 of the Constitution empowers the President to promulgate ordinances during the 
recess of Parliament. These ordinances have the same force and effect as an act of Parliament, but 
are in the nature of temporary law. 
- His ordinance-making power is coextensive as regards all matters except duration, with the law-making 
powers of the Parliament. This has two implications: 
○ An ordinance can be issued only on those subjects on which the Parliament can make laws. 
○ An ordinance is subject to the same consti tutional limitation as an act of Parliament. Hence, an 
ordinance cannot abridge or take away any of the fundamental rights. So, statement 
II is not correct. 
- An ordinance like any other legislation, can be retrospective, that is, it may come into force from 
a back date. It may modify or repeal any act of Parliament or another ordinance. It can alter or 
amend a tax law also. However, it cannot be issued to amend the Constitution. So, statements I and 
III are correct. 
Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer.

 The Wet-bulb temperature (WBT) is the lowest temperature achieved by adiabatic evaporation (= 
without adding heat or with equal enthalpy) of water in the air until the air is saturated (absolute humidity 
rises). 
 Heat is required to evaporate water. If this evaporation is adiabatic, the heat is extracted from the 
environment (e.g. the air), causing the air to cool down and become more humid, this process will 
continue to do so until the air around the system becomes saturated with water or reach the levels of 
absolute humidity. With incre asing levels of humidity this cooling effect of evaporation gets 
diminished/weakened. Thus, WBT can be taken to as a measure of effect of humidity on animals and 
environment. 
 In animals sweating is a physiological process in response to heat stress on the body, the 
sweat by means of evaporation from the skin absorbs the internal heat, leading to maintenance of body 
temperature. In situations of increased humidity, that is increased wet bulb temperatures, this cooling 
effect of sweat is lost, thus accentuating the heat stress. 
 World Bank in its Climate Risk Country Profile for India have cited that researches have 
placed a threshold of 35°C (wet bulb ambient air temperature) on the human body’s ability 
to regulate temperatur e, beyond which even a very short p eriod of exposure can present risk of 
serious ill-health and death. So, statement II is correct.

- National Electronic Fund Transfer (NEFT) and Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) are two 
electronic payment systems in India that enable the transfer of money between bank accounts. 
- RTGS is a system where there is continuous and real-time settlement of fund -transfers, 
individually on a transaction -by-transaction basis (without netting) . 'Real Time' means the 
processing of instructions at the time they are received; 'Gross Settlement' means that the settlement 
of funds transfer instructions occurs individually. 
- National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) is a nation -wide centralised payment system owned and 
operated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). 
- NEFT is an electronic fund transfer system in which the transactions received up to a 
particular time are proces sed in batches (every two hours). Contrary to this, in RTGS, the 
transactions are processed continuously on a transaction -by-transaction basis throughout the day. So,

Type of Clemency 
Meaning Effect / Example 
1. Pardon It removes both the sentence and the conviction. 
The convict is fully absolved from all punishments and disqualiﬁcations. 
2. Commutation Substitution of one form of punishment for a lighter one. 
Death sentence → Rigorous imprisonment → Simple imprisonment. 
3. Remission Reduction in the period of sentence without changing its nature. 
Rigorous imprisonment for 2 years → Reduced to 1 year. 
4. Respite Awarding a lesser sentence due to special circumstances. 
A pregnant woman given life imprisonment instead of death.

- Article 72 of the Constitution of India provides for the pardoning powers to the President. 
- In Epuru Sudhakar versus the Government of Andhra Pradesh, 2006 the Supreme Court said that 
the powers to pardon as granted to the Pres ident under Article 72 are not immune to judicial review. 
So, statement 1 is correct. 
- The court in this case emphasized that for effective exercise of these powers the reasons for providing 
or denying pardon must be mentioned. Besides, the court said that pardon obtained on the basis of 
manifest mistake or fraud can also be reviewed or cancelled. 
- The court further elaborated that if powers under Article 72 are exercised on irrelevant discriminatory 
grounds or in bad faith, then in such case the judicial review becomes necessary. 
- Also, in several cases, the SC had ruled that the President has to act on advice of the council of 
ministers while deciding pardoning powers , such cases include Maru Ram versus Union of India, 
1980 and Dhanajay Chaterjee versus State of West Bengal. So, statement 2 is not correct. 
Therefore, option (a) is the correct answer.

- Each House of Parliament has its own presiding officer. There is a Speaker and a Deputy Speaker for the 
Lok Sabha and a Chairman and a Deputy Chairman for the Rajya Sabha. A panel of chairpersons for the 
Lok Sabha and a panel of vice-chairpersons for the Rajya Sabha is also appointed. 
- The Speaker does not vacate her/his office with dissolution of the Lok Sabha but vacates his 
office immediately before the first meeting of the newly -elected Lok Sabha. Therefore, the 
President appoints a member of the Lok Sabha as the Speaker Pro Tem. Usually, the senior most member 
is selected for this. So, statement I is correct. 
- In Britain, the Speaker is strictly a non-party person because there is a convention that the Speaker has 
to resign from her/his party and remain politically neutral. This healthy convention is not fully established 
in India where the Speaker does not resign from the membership of her/his party on her/his 
election to the exalted office. So, statement II is not correct. 
- The Speaker is provided with a security of tenure. He can be removed only by a resolution passed by 
the Lok Sabha by a special majority (ie, a majority of all the then members of the House) and 
not by an ordinary majority (ie, a majority of the members present and voting in the House). This motion 
of removal can be considered and discussed onl y when it has the support of at least 50 members. 
Additionally, a procedural safeguard is embedded in the process: any such resolution can be introduced 
only after giving a minimum of 14 days' prior notice, ensuring sufficient time for thorough 
deliberation and informed decision-making. So, statement III is correct. 
Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer

In India, the minerals are classified as minor minerals and major minerals. “Minor Minerals” means building

Nature Restoration Law (NRL): 
- It is a European Union (EU) law to tackle the triple crises of climate change, biodiversity loss, and 
environmental degradation. 
- It is the first continent -wide, comprehensive law of its kind . It is a key element of the EU 
Biodiversity Strategy, which sets binding targets to restore degraded ecosystems, in particular those with 
the most potential to capture and store carbon and to prevent and reduce the impact of natural disasters. 
- Under the NRL, Member States will have to restore at least 20% of the EU’s land and sea by 
2030, including terrestrial, coastal, and freshwater, forest, agricultural, and urban areas. 
- By 2050, the measures should extend to all ecosystems "requiring restoration". The EU NRL also targets 
an obligation to improve urban green spaces, contribute to free -flowing rivers by removing artificial 
barriers, increase pollinator populations, and contribute to the target of 3 billion additional trees 
throughout the EU. 
- Member States must ado pt "restoration plans" detailing how they intend to achieve these targets and 
ensure that the restored areas do not significantly deteriorate. 
- While drafting these Nature Restoration Plans, Member States also need to consider socio -
economic impacts and benefits and estimate the financial needs for its implementation. 
Therefore, option (a) is the correct answer.

 Statement 2 is correct. The GAGAN is designed to provide the additional accuracy, availability,

necessary

to

for

of
 
ﬂight,

route
 
through

qualiﬁed
 
airports
 
within
 
the

service
 
volume.

increased
 
accuracy
 
in
 
position
 
reporting,
 
allowing

more
 
uniform
 
and

Air

including
 
maritime,
 
highways,

- GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation (GAGAN) uses a system of ground stations to provide 
necessary augmentations to the GPS standard positioning service(SPS) navigation signal. 
- The GAGAN is designed to provide the additional accuracy, availability, and integrity necessary 
to enable users to rely on GPS for all phases of flight , from en route through approach for all 
qualified airports within the GAGAN service volume. So, statement 1 is correct. 
- GAGAN will also provide the capability for increased accuracy in position reporting, allowing for 
more uniform and high-quality Air Traffic Management (ATM). So, statement 2 is correct. 
- In addition, GAGAN will provide benefits beyond aviation to all modes of transportation, 
including maritime, highways, and railroads. So, statement 3 is not correct. 
- A network of precisely surveyed ground reference stations (INdianReference Stations INRES) is 
strategically positioned across the country to collect GPS satellite data. Using this information, the master 
control centre (INdian Master Control Centre INMCC) generates messages to correct any signal errors. 
These correction messages are then uplinked through (INdian Land Uplink Station INLUS) and broadcast 
through communication satellites (Geostationary) to receivers onboard aircraft using the same frequency 
as GPS. 
Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

- Gukesh Dommaraju has made history by becoming the youngest chess world champion after defeating 
defending champion Ding Liren of China in the final match of their series held in Singapore. So, 
statement 1 is not correct. 
- Abhimanyu Mishra from America became the youngest international master in 2019 at the age of 
10 and began earning his GM norms in 2021. So, statement 2 is correct.
